Waist-to-Height Ratio Calculator

Divide your waist measurement by your height to get a simple screening ratio. Keeping the waist below half of height is a commonly used practical guide.

Educational estimates only. Results are not medical advice, a diagnosis, or a treatment plan. Talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your health. Read the full medical disclaimer.

Example: 170

Height

How to use this calculator

  1. Choose metric or imperial units.
  2. Measure your waist with a tape: find the bottom of your ribs and the top of your hips, wrap the tape midway between them, and measure after breathing out normally.
  3. Enter your height and waist, then press Calculate.

The formulas

Waist-to-height ratio = waist circumference ÷ height, using the same units for both (for example, both in cm or both in inches).

Ratio bands used on this page, from NICE guideline NG246: 0.40–0.49 healthy central fat; 0.50–0.59 increased; 0.60 or more high.

Limits of this measure

This ratio is a screening estimate, not a diagnosis. The NICE and NHS guidance applies it to adults and notes it is not suitable in some situations, such as a growth disorder or a BMI over 35. If you are unsure, ask a healthcare professional.

Frequently asked questions

Why is 0.5 the threshold?

A ratio under 0.5 (waist less than half of height) is a commonly used practical screening threshold, and NICE advises people to try to keep their waist to less than half their height. It is a guide, not a diagnosis.

How do I measure my waist?

Find the bottom of your ribs and the top of your hips, wrap a tape measure around your middle halfway between them, and measure after breathing out naturally.

Can I mix cm and inches?

No. Waist and height must use the same units. The calculator converts for you when you pick a unit system.

Does a high ratio mean I am ill?

No. It suggests extra fat around the middle may be worth discussing with a professional. It cannot diagnose any condition.
